messages:
Emily Tran: Hi @people-ops — quick update and a few questions. Our baby arrived early (33w) and is in the NICU. I was on primary parental leave scheduled to end 2030-06-15, but baby likely won’t be discharged until later. Is there a process to extend paid leave or get a temporary pay top-up for NICU stays? Also want to coordinate a phased return and oncall coverage. What paperwork do I need and how fast can we move?

Bernice (People Ops): Hey Emily, so sorry to hear that — sending hugs. :heart: We do have a NICU/medical-extension workflow. Short answer: we can approve additional paid leave or a company pay-top-up for NICU when we receive medical documentation. Steps below.

Bernice (People Ops): 1) Please submit the NICU discharge estimate or physician note via the secure form: https://intra.redwood/hr/forms/medical-leave-extension (select "NICU/early birth").
2) Complete the short-term disability (STD) election if you want wage replacement while out (STD can run concurrently with parental leave in some cases).
3) People Ops will file the extension and, if eligible, apply our parental top-up policy (up to 6 additional weeks at full pay for primary parents with NICU).
4) Payroll processes the top-up the next payroll cycle after approval.

Bernice (People Ops): Can you DM the estimated discharge date when you have it? We'll start the paperwork immediately.

Emily Tran: Thank you — I uploaded the note to the secure form just now (submission id `nicu-2030-0007`). Estimated discharge is 2030-06-28 but could move.

Payroll Bot: Thanks @Emily Tran, received submission `nicu-2030-0007`. Payroll note: if People Ops approves on or before 2030-06-10 we can include the top-up in the 2030-06-15 payroll run; otherwise it will appear on the following run. Please allow one payroll cycle for adjustments. Taxes/withholdings follow standard payroll rules.

Jamie R (Eng Manager): Emily — the team and I can cover your scope. Suggesting Sarah take primary oncall for the next 4 weeks and we bring on a short-term contractor for the two backlog projects. Budget-wise I have headroom in my team allocation to cover contractor hours for up to 8 weeks.

Sarah L (Eng): I can swap oncall with Sam for weekdays, happy to handle the pager for that window. I’ll update the runbook and mark any open PRs that need attention.

Sam (Oncall): If Sarah is on weekdays I can cover weekend pager. I pushed a small automation to reduce noisy alerts: `scripts/reduce-noise.sh` — please review.

Lucy (Legal): Quick legal/consent note: when you submit medical docs we need a signed consent to store/handle PHI in our HR system. Bernice, can you send the standard release? Emily, we'll keep access tightly scoped to People Ops + Payroll + Legal for this case.

Bernice (People Ops): On it. Emily, sending the release link now (secure): https://intra.redwood/hr/consent/2030-nicu. Sign electronically and we'll attach it to the case.

Emily Tran: Got it, signed the consent. One more Q: equipment — my laptop was due back on 2030-06-20 per checkout policy. Can we extend checkout while I'm out?

Bernice (People Ops): Yes — we can extend the company device checkout while you're on approved leave. No need to ship back until 2 weeks after you return. We'll flag your asset ID to prevent auto-collection.

Jamie R (Eng Manager): For ramp/back-to-work — Emily, would you prefer: A) 3 weeks half-time (reduced meetings, deep work mornings), or B) 4 weeks 60% FTE? We can make either work and keep your oncall coverage until fully comfortable.

Emily Tran: I think option A sounds good. I’ll plan for half-time for the first 3 weeks and then re-evaluate.

Bernice (People Ops): Noted. We'll record a phased return plan: start date TBD, 3 weeks at 50% then full-time. Please DM expected start-of-ramp when you have it and we'll set a formal accommodation in the system.

Payroll Bot: Reminder: phased return pay follows actual hours; top-ups only apply while on approved leave (not during part-time ramp). If you want partial pay support during ramp, we can explore a short-term accommodation — ping @Bernice for details.

Lucy (Legal): Also note FMLA/CFRA (if applicable) interplay — medical extensions for NICU are typically protected but we need to ensure documentation supports job-protected leave if you want that coverage. Bernice will coordinate.

Bernice (People Ops): Action items — I’ll: 1) approve provisional NICU extension upon consent + note; 2) notify Payroll to queue top-up; 3) create a phased return accommodation record; 4) set a 15-min sync with Emily + Jamie tomorrow to confirm oncall/resourcing.

Emily Tran: Thank you all, really appreciate the quick help.

Jamie R (Eng Manager): Sending resources and a short handover template in the thread for the contractor. Will update the calendar for oncall swaps. :thumbsup:

HR Forms Bot: Auto-confirmation: Form `nicu-2030-0007` and consent `2030-nicu` attached to case #PO-2030-78. People Ops will reach out within 24 hours.

Bernice (People Ops): Closing loop — created the case and scheduled the sync. Emily, we’ve flagged parental top-up as provisional — final approval after medical review, but looks eligible from docs. Reach out anytime.
